title: Design System: It's Okay It's Official

headline.purpose: "Hi, I’m Alex." on the back of the tape.

body.purpose: The note on the back of the tape: paragraphs and links.

note.purpose: Pencil margin notes on the tape, and the A.P. sign-off.

pencil-action.purpose: Underlined pencil words that act: Turn over, Put down.

aside.purpose: A one- or two-word gloss beside a printed line (today, last time).

key.purpose: Number and function legends on the keycaps.

key-operator.purpose: Plus and total legends on the double-height keys.

brand.purpose: The IOIO wordmark on the maker plate.

label.purpose: Silk-screened housing labels such as Sound and Proof 12.

shadows.name: paper-drop
shadows.purpose: The tape as a whole (applied as a filter).

shadows.name: paper-curl
shadows.purpose: Side edges of every tape line.

shadows.name: keycap-pressed
shadows.purpose: Any key while pressed, over its own lip colour.

shadows.name: print-slot
shadows.purpose: The dark mouth the tape enters.

shadows.name: loose-paper
shadows.purpose: The skip-link scrap and other loose paper.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Switch knob, skip scrap, tear-bar lift, and turning a torn strip over (760ms).

motion.name: paper-feed
motion.value: steps(n, jump-start), about 7px and 24ms per step (12ms when backlogged)
motion.purpose: The tape advancing after each print; never a glide.

motion.name: print-sweep
motion.value: 140ms + 1.6ms per dot, max 420ms, left to right
motion.purpose: The print head striking a line column by column.

motion.name: pencil-write
motion.value: 38ms per character + 60ms between words, linear clip reveal
motion.purpose: Pencil notes appearing word by word.

motion.name: pencil-stroke
motion.purpose: Ticks, arrows, and the double rule drawing on.

motion.name: tear-flight
motion.value: 1150ms cubic-bezier(.2,.8,.2,1); flip rotateY(180deg) from 28% on cubic-bezier(.45,0,.2,1)
motion.purpose: A torn strip flying to rest and turning over.

motion.name: put-down
motion.purpose: A torn strip leaving off the left edge.

components.name: Number Key
components.description: Pale keycap on a solid lip; travels 2px when pressed.
components.css: .ds-key { display: inline-grid; place-content: center; gap: 3px; width: var(--kw, 64px); height: var(--kh, 48px); border: 0; border-radius: 9px; font: 600 20px/1 "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: translate 70ms ease-out, box-shadow 70ms ease-out; background: var(--key, #e8e7e2); color: var(--key-ink, #24272b); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.75), inset 0 -2px 0 rgb(0 0 0 / 0.07), 0 3px 0 var(--key-lo, #a3a29b), 0 5px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.38); } .ds-key:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-key:active { translate: 0 2px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.5), 0 1px 0 var(--key-lo, #a3a29b), 0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35); } .ds-key:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--paper, #f7f7f3); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Function Key
components.description: Slate keycap for divide, multiply, minus, and plus.
components.css: .ds-key-fn { display: inline-grid; place-content: center; gap: 3px; width: var(--kw, 64px); height: var(--kh, 48px); border: 0; border-radius: 9px; font: 600 20px/1 "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: translate 70ms ease-out, box-shadow 70ms ease-out; background: var(--fn, #474b51); color: var(--fn-ink, #eef0ec); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.14), 0 3px 0 var(--fn-lo, #2a2d31), 0 5px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.38); } .ds-key-fn:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-key-fn:active { translate: 0 2px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.1), 0 1px 0 var(--fn-lo, #2a2d31), 0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35); } .ds-key-fn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--paper, #f7f7f3); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Total Key
components.description: The only red cap on the machine; every total earns a pencil note.
components.css: .ds-key-total { display: inline-grid; place-content: center; gap: 3px; width: var(--kw, 64px); height: var(--kh, 48px); border: 0; border-radius: 9px; font: 600 20px/1 "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; cursor: pointer; transition: translate 70ms ease-out, box-shadow 70ms ease-out; height: calc(2 * var(--kh, 48px) + var(--kg, 10px)); background: var(--ink-red, #b8322a); color: #fff4ef; font-size: 26px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.28), 0 3px 0 #741c16, 0 5px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.38); } .ds-key-total small { font: 700 8px/1 "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; } .ds-key-total:hover { filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-key-total:active { translate: 0 2px; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.2), 0 1px 0 #741c16, 0 2px 4px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35); } .ds-key-total:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--paper, #f7f7f3); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Pencil Button
components.description: An action written on paper: underlined graphite words, no box.
components.css: .ds-paper { background: var(--paper, #f7f7f3); padding: 18px 20px; } .ds-pencil-btn { padding: 4px 2px; border: 0; background: none; color: var(--graphite, #4a4e55); font: 400 19px/1 "Pen", "Bradley Hand", "Segoe Print", cursive; text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.2em; cursor: pointer; } .ds-pencil-btn:hover { color: var(--ink, #1c1d22); } .ds-pencil-btn:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--graphite, #4a4e55); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Paper Link
components.description: A written-out address on the back of the tape.
components.css: .ds-verso { margin: 0; padding: 20px 22px; background: var(--paper, #f7f7f3); font: 400 19px/1.06 "Pen", "Bradley Hand", "Segoe Print", cursive; } .ds-link { color: var(--ink, #1c1d22); text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 0.2em; overflow-wrap: break-word; } .ds-link:hover { color: var(--ink-red, #b8322a); } .ds-link:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--graphite, #4a4e55); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 2px; }

components.name: Skip Scrap
components.description: The page's only navigation: a scrap of paper that slides in on focus.
components.css: .ds-skip { display: inline-block; padding: 8px 14px 10px; background: var(--paper, #f7f7f3); color: var(--graphite, #4a4e55); font: 400 21px/1 "Pen", "Bradley Hand", "Segoe Print", cursive; text-decoration: none; box-shadow: 2px 8px 18px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.4); } .ds-skip:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--paper, #f7f7f3); outline-offset: 3px; }

components.name: Sound Switch
components.description: A silk-screened slide switch on the housing; off by default.
components.css: .ds-housing { padding: 16px 20px; background: var(--machine, #25282c); border-radius: 12px; } .ds-switch { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 6px 0 6px 8px; border: 0; background: none; color: var(--label, #a7adb4); font: 600 10px/1 "Helvetica Neue", Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif; letter-spacing: 0.22em; text-transform: uppercase; cursor: pointer; } .ds-switch-track { position: relative; width: 30px; height: 14px; border-radius: 7px; background: #121416; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 3px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.85); } .ds-switch-knob { position: absolute; top: 2px; left: 2px; width: 14px; height: 10px; border-radius: 4px; background: linear-gradient(#dfe2e5, #9aa0a6); transition: translate 180ms cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-switch[aria-checked="true"] { color: #eef0f2; } .ds-switch[aria-checked="true"] .ds-switch-knob { translate: 12px 0; background: linear-gradient(#ffd9cf, #e0705e); } .ds-switch:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--paper, #f7f7f3); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 4px; }

components.name: Tape With Pencil Note
components.description: Bond paper on felt carrying a graphite margin note, as written after a total.
components.html: Me: Alex Pugh. Dir., AI ops, Insight.
components.css: .ds-felt { padding: 24px; background: var(--felt, #1c3d31); } .ds-tape { width: var(--tape, 224px); background: var(--paper, #f7f7f3); box-shadow: inset 7px 0 7px -7px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.09), inset -7px 0 7px -7px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.09); filter: drop-shadow(1px 7px 9px rgb(0 0 0 / 0.32)); } .ds-note { margin: 0; padding: 0.2em 16px 0.55em 18px; color: var(--graphite, #4a4e55); font: 400 19px/1.02 "Pen", "Bradley Hand", "Segoe Print", cursive; rotate: -0.5deg; transform-origin: 0 50%; }

narrative.overview:
The site is one object on one desk: a graphite IOIO Proof 12 printing calculator under a warm lamp, its single strip of bright bond paper running from the top of the screen down into the print slot, across a bottle-green felt blotter. Nothing is interface chrome. Every surface is a material with a job: felt is the ground, paper carries the record, the housing holds the controls, the LCD reflects, graphite signs off. Every control is either a part of the machine (keycaps, a sound switch, a serrated tear bar) or a word written in pencil on paper.

Two hands make every mark, and they never trade places. The machine prints level, flush-right 5x7 dot-matrix figures through a two-colour ribbon, black for entries and red for subtractions, negatives and errors, and it advances the paper in hard mechanical steps. The person answers in graphite: a script note, a tick beside a total, a double rule under the final one, each set slightly askew and written a word at a time. Density is low and the palette is quiet so that each printed line and each pencil mark lands as an event.

The world refuses the about-me profile card and the generative canvas with a name in the corner. Who Alex is arrives as pencil marginalia on a working tape, and the full note is written on the back of the strip once it is torn off.
keyCharacteristics: One bottle-green felt ground under a single overhead lamp; everything else is a physical object resting on it.
One accent: ribbon red, owned by the total key and by red print.
Two voices on fixed media: dot-matrix print and silk-screened Helvetica for the machine, graphite Pen script for the person.
Square-cut and torn paper edges, softly rounded plastic keys, a housing rounded only at the top.
Real key travel, a stepped paper feed and a word-by-word pencil, all of which collapse to their end state under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Two-Ribbon Rule
rules.body: The print head has exactly two inks. Ribbon Black prints entries, date and time stamps, clears and positive totals; Ribbon Red prints subtractions, negative figures and errors. Red never prints for emphasis.

rules.name: The One Red Key Rule
rules.body: The total key is the only red cap on the machine. Every other key is pale or slate.

rules.name: The Material Ground Rule
rules.body: Felt is the only background. Anything placed on it is an object with its own material and its own shadow; nothing floats on the felt as a tinted panel.

rules.name: The Two Hands Rule
rules.body: The machine speaks in dot-matrix print and Helvetica on the housing; the person speaks in Pen script in graphite. Helvetica never appears on paper, and the pencil never writes on the machine.

rules.name: The Grain Rule
rules.body: Pencil that is read (notes, asides, ticks, rules, arrows, the back of the tape) passes through the shared graphite filter: fractal-noise displacement plus a paper-tooth mask, so it reads as pencil on fibre rather than a vector line. Pencil that is pressed (links, pencil buttons, the skip scrap) stays crisp.

rules.name: The Overhead Lamp Rule
rules.body: There is one light, above the desk. Every shadow falls down the screen, highlights sit on top edges, and wells darken from the top. A shadow cast upward or sideways belongs to a different lamp.

rules.name: The Key Travel Rule
rules.body: Every key stands on a solid 3px lip in its own darker shade and travels 2px when pressed, its lip shrinking to 1px, in 70ms. Hover only brightens a key slightly (brightness 1.06), and only on devices that can hover.

rules.name: The Level Print Rule
rules.body: What the machine makes sits dead level: print, LCD, keys, housing. Only the hand and loose paper tilt: notes between -1.1 and 0.4 degrees, ticks between -9 and 5 degrees, a torn strip at rest between -0.6 and -3.6 degrees.

dos: **Do** keep Bottle-Green Felt (#1c3d31) as the only background, with its lamp glow, vignette and grain.
**Do** print machine output only as 5x7 dot matrix in Ribbon Black or Ribbon Red, flush right, with its symbol in the last column.
**Do** write the person's voice in Pen and Pencil Graphite, and draw new pencil marks as round-capped strokes through the graphite filter.
**Do** make every new control a machine part (keycap, switch, tear bar) or an underlined pencil word on paper.
**Do** use a 2px Bond Paper focus ring on the machine and a 2px Pencil Graphite ring on paper.
**Do** keep every keycap legend at 4.5:1 or better against its cap.
**Do** deliver the end state at once under reduced motion: lines already printed, notes already written, ticks already drawn, a torn strip already at rest.
donts: **Don't** introduce a new hue; every colour is a desk material or the ribbon's red.
**Don't** add a second red cap to the machine, or print in red for emphasis.
**Don't** round, border or tint paper; its edges are cut square or torn into 9px teeth.
**Don't** set Helvetica on paper or Pen on the machine.
**Don't** imitate the dot matrix on the page with a monospace or pixel webfont.
**Don't** feed the tape smoothly; it advances in steps.
**Don't** present the bio as a profile card or sign a generative canvas with a name in the corner; the bio is pencil on the back of a torn tape.
**Don't** use brand icons or logos for links; write the addresses out.
**Don't** use pure white or pure black as an on-screen surface or text colour.
